item.title: My (very) fast zero-allocation webserver using OxCaml
item.description:
📝 Given an input buffer like this, what can we do with OxCaml vs vanilla OCaml to make this go fast. OxCaml advances this by providing unboxed versions of small numbers that live in registers or on the stack, via a new syntax int16#. That failed, but it did reveal that we have this intriguing int16 pair layout instead of the normal OCaml flat value representation.
🔗 Read more: https://anil.recoil.org/notes/oxcaml-httpz

item.title: EU launches government satcom program in sovereignty push
item.description:
📝 BRUSSELS — The European Union’s new government satellite communications program, GOVSATCOM, which pools capacity from eight already on-orbit geosynchronous satellites, began operations last week, European Commissioner for Defence and Space Andrius Kubilius said Jan. “Last week we started GOVSATCOM operations,” Kubilius said during his opening remarks at the European Space Conference. Concerning IRIS2, the commissioner also said that IRIS² Ka-band military frequencies were brought into use last week.
🔗 Read more: https://spacenews.com/eu-launches-government-satcom-program-in-sovereignty-push/

item.title: Library of Juggling
item.description:
📝 For every trick found in the Library, there will be an animated representation of the pattern created via JugglingLab, in addition to general information about the trick (siteswap, difficulty level, prerequisite tricks, etc. I will also include links to other tutorials for the trick that can be found online, ranging from YouTube videos to private sites like this one. Recent Additions (6/13/15): Crossed-Arm Shower Reverse Crossed-Arm Shower Frostbite (submitted by Andrew Olson) Ripley's Rainbow Zebra Factory Update Log The Library of Juggling is on an indefinite hiatus, which means no new tricks will be added.
🔗 Read more: https://libraryofjuggling.com/
